submission.natural_language_explanation: A broad, near-default-on GELU-dip pole: it reaches its ~0.17 ceiling on relational/'phrase-open' tokens of running prose (finite verbs, prepositions, coordinating conjunctions, mid-sentence commas, copulas, and many adjectives/word-pieces), and is silent (pre-activation positive) on tokens that complete a noun phrase or clause: content nouns and names after a determiner, 'the', sentence-final '.', and most short code tokens. Very strongly driven tokens (pre-activation below about -1.5, e.g. some verbs like 'brings', 'Override') fall back to ~0.06 because GELU's negative lobe is non-monotone.
rival_explanations: Pure part-of-speech reading: the pole fires on every verb, preposition and conjunction regardless of context and on nothing else, so it should also fire on 'of' in 'a cup of' and never on adjectives or commas.

Anti-noun-phrase-head reading: the pole is simply the complement of a noun/determiner detector, firing on any token that is not a noun, name, 'the' or final punctuation, including code operators and brackets.

Het “winkeltje” komt al aardig vol te liggen met keukengerei. De bakken zijn bijna allemaal gevuld. Dat is maar goed ook want de zon schijnt en moeder muis wil graag met de grote schoonmaak beginnen.
In de "winkel" zie je: houten tobbes en zinken emmers
de zwabbers, mattenkloppers en vegers zijn handwerk en op maat gemaakt voor familie muis
theedoeken, poetsdoeken, vaatdoekjes, stofdoeken
Persil voor de handwas, Brasso voor het echte poetswerk, Sunlight zeep en afwasborstels voor de vaat, een busje Vim om het aanrecht schoon te maken en handvegertjes
natuurlijk ontbreken spons en zeem (van echt zeemleer) niet in de keuken van familie muis.
Binnenkort is het keukengerei in verschillende setjes in de webwinkel te koop.
Het keukenfornuis met schouw is klaar. Het lepelrekje hangt en de ‘’emaillen” pannen staan op het fornuis. In het keukengerei zijn kleine gaatjes geboord zodat de lepels en deegroller aan het lepelrekje kunnen hangen.Op de schouw staat een houten botervat.
Het aanrecht, de kastjes en het fornuis staan in een decor (een holletje). Een muizenhol heeft natuurlijk meerdere gangen en vertrekken. Ik heb het decor zo gemaakt dat je het zowel voor de keuken als voor de kraamkamer kunt gebruiken. De achterzijde van het decor kun je als kraamkamer gebruiken en de voorzijde kun je gebruiken om de keuken in te richten. Je kunt het decor naast het muizenhuis neer zetten.
Zelf vind ik het erg mooi om aan beide zijden van het muizenhuis een holletje te maken. Aan de linkerzijde de kraamkamer en aan de rechterzijde de keuken met in het midden het muizenhuis en de bedjes voor de kinderen.
Aan de beschrijving van het patroonboekje en het samenstellen van de materiaalpakketjes
wordt gewerkt!

Abstract : In quantum field theories defined on a spacetime with boundaries, the entanglement entropy exhibits subleading, boundary-induced corrections to the ubiquitous area law. At critical points described by conformal field theories (CFTs), and when the entangling surface intersects the physical boundary of the space, new universal terms appear in the entropy and encode valuable information about the boundary CFT (BCFT). In $2+1$ dimensions, the universal subleading boundary term is logarithmic with coefficient $b(\theta)$ depending on the angle $\theta$ at which the entangling surface intersects the boundary, as well as on the boundary conditions (BCs). In this paper, we conduct a numerical study of $b(\theta)$ for free bosons on finite-size square lattices. We find a surprisingly accurate fit between our lattice results and the corresponding holographic function available in the literature. We also comment on the ratio $b^{\prime\prime}(\pi/2)/A_T$, where $A_T$ is the central charge in the near boundary expansion of the stress tensor, for which a holographic analysis suggests that it may be a universal quantity. We show evidence that this ratio is violated for the free boson with Dirichlet BCs.

One of the great things about music is that everyone can find something they like. In many cases, we may like more than one genre. It is a universal pleasure, something that can bring us all together rather than most things that seem to force us apart.
And there are so many different types of songs, the mood, the tempo, the style, and even the meaning. There is so much to be explored, understood, and appreciated. And, quite often, they overlap.
What can be classified as one thing can often also be called another. So, let’s break it down a little by starting at the beginning…

The Origins of Music
You might think that its origins might be relatively easy to determine, but that is not the case. Scholars fiercely debate when and how our love of music started. Some think that it may have started with the beginnings of language, others at a later date.
They certainly evolved from mythical beliefs and were present around 40,000 BC because we have remnants of flutes made from bone. But where, when, and how exactly is unknown.
There were instruments in the Xia Dynasty in about 2000 BC. And, in the civilizations in the Indus Valley, again in the Bronze age period about 2500 BC.
Did Writing Help?
Once we had learned formal writing skills that could be understood by others, music certainly changed in substance and complexity. Formalized music was seen in the so-called “literate civilizations.”
These are Greek, Egyptian, Persian, Indian, Chinese, and Middle-eastern cultures. One of the great steps forward was taken in 600 BC. This was when the Greek philosopher and mathematician Pythagoras identified music as being scientific and having an order.
He might have been famous for his ‘right-angled triangle’ theorem. But, for musicians, he is more famous for observing and creating the octave.
What Was Its Use?
Not for pleasure at that time. It was ceremonial, used as appreciation for any one of thousands of deities, depending on the religion. It also observed, gave reverence, and sometimes promoted fear of mythical figures. There was a point, though, where it became a little more serious.
The Medieval Period
Many people in the western world treat other geographical areas and their music as irrelevant. Of course, it isn’t, and it developed just as it did in Western cultures. But, it is western music we are dealing with here. So, it is there, with respect to the other cultures and their music, that I will be concentrating on.

Nirudi nyuma kidogo, Kuna mdogo wangu yuko katika kundi moja la fesibuku, la wasichana na wanawake, amekuwa akinisimulia visa kadha wa kadha vinavyowatokea wadada wengi walio kwenye ndoa.
Mambo mengi ambayo huwa hunisimulia hunifanya nijue kumbe kweli UKIMWI bado upo na unaua. Kuna kisa fulani aliniambia miezi kadhaa iliyopita, kikanifanya nitamani kama watu wengi zaidi wangeelewa uhalisia wa huu ugonjwa na jinsi unavyowamaliza wengi mpaka leo hii, hata wale wasiotegemea.
Mbaya zaidi kwa sasa ambapo kumekuwa na dawa za kuongeza kinga, wagonjwa wengi wa UKIMWI hawajulikani kwa kuonekana kwa macho, na huo umekuwa mtego kwa watu wengi.
Kuna binti mmoja, nitampa jina la Vero, kwenye hilo kundi ana ndoa ya miaka mitatu na wana mtoto mmoja, aliwahi kufuma jumbe za mapenzi kwenye simu ya mume wake, mwanaume akawa akijitetea na kuomba msamaha, binti akasamehe.
Siku moja binti aliamua kufuatilia namba, alipofuma tena ujumbe wa mapenzi kwa mume wake, akaja kugundua kumbe ni ya jirani yao, cha kumshangaza zaidi huyo jirani yao ni kijana wa kiume.
Binti akachanganyikiwa ndipo akaamua kuomba ushauri kwenye hilo kundi, pasipo kujitaja jina lake, watu wakamshauri asamehe, asimfuatilie mwanaume, wengine wakashauri aachane naye, na kuna waliomshauri akapime na akikutwa salama basi amuache.
